title: Redundancy Test Against Existing TrustEngine Mechanisms

reference_mechanisms.EWMA_magnitude: E_t = beta * A_t + (1 - beta) * E_{t-1} (tracks mean anomaly magnitude)
reference_mechanisms.Slow_burn_accumulator: SB_t = max(0, SB_{t-1} - delta) + 1.0 * I(E_t > gamma)
reference_mechanisms.Sliding_window: Counting events in fixed horizon W

Family_A.status: NON-REDUNDANT with EWMA, but REDUNDANT with cumulative epoch counter
Family_A.justification: Counts events above q without magnitude scaling. Differs fundamentally from E_t. However, it is mathematically identical to a standard cumulative event counter.

Family_B.status: REDUNDANT if f(A_t) is linear; NON-REDUNDANT if f(A_t) is non-linear
Family_B.justification: If f(A_t) = k * A_t, then Q_{t+1} = rho * Q_t + k * A_t. Setting rho = 1 - beta and k = beta makes Q_t mathematically identical to E_t. Even with different rho, it remains an EWMA of anomaly score, merely operating at a different timescale. It does not introduce a novel representational dimension.

Family_C.justification: Family C incorporates a non-linear threshold offset: f(A_t) = max(0, A_t - q_low) / (A_thr - q_low). This contains two non-linear elements absent from E_t: (1) a lower deadband [0, q_low] that completely zeroes out standard benign traffic, and (2) normalization relative to the decision boundary A_thr. This is not an EWMA of A_t, cannot be obtained by reparameterizing E_t, and is not a sliding-window count.

Family_D.justification: Operates on inter-arrival time Delta_t = t - t_last rather than anomaly score magnitude. Completely distinct from E_t, SB_t, and sliding windows.

Family_E.justification: Exact sliding window rate Q_t = (1/W) sum I(A >= q) is textbook sliding-window detection. The EMA approximation is mathematically identical to Family B with binary input.
